findings.explanation: The workflow sets a safe top-level `permissions: read-all`, then overrides it with `write-all` on every job. publish-dockerhub runs two third-party actions (elgohr/Publish-Docker-Github-Action, peter-evans/dockerhub-description) that hold the Docker Hub password, and update-scoop only dispatches an event using a separate PAT, so neither needs any GITHUB_TOKEN write scope. A compromised action or a tag-triggered run gets a token that can write contents, packages, actions, workflows and security events. holden did not flag this because the scan_roots target filter does not cover the workflows (see HOLDEN_AI_004).
findings.fix:
# jobs.goreleaser (line 12)
permissions:
  contents: write
# jobs.publish-dockerhub (line 44)
permissions:
  contents: read
# jobs.update-scoop (line 66)
permissions:
  contents: read
findings.remediation: Grant per-job least privilege: goreleaser needs `contents: write`; publish-dockerhub needs `contents: read`; update-scoop needs `contents: read` (or `{}`).
findings.title: Release workflow grants write-all GITHUB_TOKEN to all three jobs, including ones running third-party actions with Docker Hub credentials

findings.explanation: HLD_DF_008 and HLD_DF_018 flag the `curl -k` and `| sh` individually, but the composition is worse: the build resolves `releases/latest` at build time, downloads the `linux_386` tarball with TLS verification off, and extracts it into /usr/bin with no sha256 or GPG check, although goreleaser already publishes checksums.txt and a detached signature. The image is tagged with the release version in release.yml but contains whatever `latest` is when it builds, so it is not reproducible and an older tag can ship a newer binary. The binary deletes BigTable rows using whatever credentials the container is given, and it is the 386 build regardless of the host architecture.
findings.remediation: Build the binary into the image from the tagged release instead of downloading it: pass the version as a build arg (`ARG VERSION`), download `crusher_${VERSION}_linux_<arch>.tar.gz` and checksums.txt over verified TLS, run `sha256sum -c`, and select the architecture with TARGETARCH. Alternatively use a multi-stage build or `COPY` the goreleaser-built binary from `dist/` (goreleaser `dockers`).
findings.title: Docker image installs an unverified, unpinned 'latest' crusher binary, ignoring the signed checksums the release already publishes

findings.explanation: The action is SHA-pinned, but it downloads whichever goreleaser binary is newest at release time, and that step holds the GPG key, passphrase and the Homebrew tap token. ci.yml's snapshot job pins `'~> v2'`, so CI does not exercise the version that the release actually uses and a new goreleaser major can break or compromise a release with no prior signal.
findings.remediation: Pin the release job to the same constraint as CI (`'~> v2'`) or to an exact version, and bump both together.
findings.title: Release job runs goreleaser `version: latest` while CI pins `~> v2`

findings.explanation: holden's valid targets are terraform, dockerfile, k8s, compose, gha and gitlab; `ghat` is the name of the sibling tool, not a target. A no-path `holden scan` reported findings only for the two Dockerfiles, so none of the six workflow files were evaluated, which is why the `write-all` permissions in release.yml went unreported. Confidence is medium because holden's handling of an unknown target name was not confirmed directly.
findings.remediation: Change the target to `gha`, then re-run `holden scan` and triage what the workflows produce.
findings.title: .holden.yaml scan_roots lists target `ghat`, so GitHub Actions workflows are not scanned

findings.explanation: The key is already imported into the runner's keyring by ghaction-import-gpg, and .goreleaser.yml references only `.Env.PASSPHRASE` and `.Env.GPG_FINGERPRINT`. Exporting the armored private key into the environment of goreleaser and every process it spawns (build hooks, sbom/syft, signing) widens its exposure for no benefit.
findings.fix:
# remove from env of the 'Run GoReleaser' step:
GPG_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
findings.remediation: Delete the `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` line from the Run GoReleaser env block.
findings.title: GPG private key is passed to the goreleaser step although only the passphrase and fingerprint are used

findings.explanation: The CLI only defines `clip` and `version` (main.go), but the GitHub-Actions branch of the entrypoint runs `crusher label -f "$INPUT_FILE" "$flags"`, which looks copied from a sibling tool. Using the image as an action always fails, and it passes an empty-string argument via the quoted `$flags`. The non-Actions branch (`crusher "$@"`) works.
findings.remediation: Either remove the Actions branch and always exec `/usr/bin/crusher "$@"`, or map action inputs to `clip` flags. Use `exec` so the exit code and signals propagate.
findings.title: entrypoint.sh calls a nonexistent `crusher label` subcommand when run under GitHub Actions

findings.explanation: The two files are identical (verified with cmp) and nothing in the repo references Dockerfile.backup. It doubles every Dockerfile finding (all four HLD_DF policies fire in both files, 8 findings for 4 issues) and any fix will have to be applied twice or the copies will drift.
findings.remediation: Delete Dockerfile.backup (git history already holds old versions), or add it to ignore_paths in .holden.yaml if it must stay.
findings.title: Dockerfile.backup is a byte-identical, unreferenced copy of Dockerfile

findings.explanation: The job has no step that generates or checks docs, so it burns a runner on every pull request and reads as coverage that does not exist.
findings.remediation: Remove the job, or add the intended docs check step.
findings.title: pr.yml `docs` job only checks out and installs Go, then does nothing
